title: Exact pairs detecting zero objects detect isomorphisms
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D,\mathcal E$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian], and let $J:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ and $I:\mathcal C\to\mathcal E$ be functors preserving zero morphisms, finite limits and finite colimits [def-galois-exact-functor]. A zero object here is an object both initial and terminal. Assume that for every $M\in\mathcal C$, if $JM$ and $IM$ are zero objects, then $M$ is a zero object. For any objects $M,N\in\mathcal C$ and any morphism $c:M\to N$, if $J(c)$ and $I(c)$ are isomorphisms, then $c$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Choose the kernel K and cokernel Q of c in the abelian category [def-sp-abelian]. The finite-limit and finite-colimit assumptions [def-galois-exact-functor] give the comparison isomorphisms F(K) ≅ kernel(F(c)) and F(Q) ≅ cokernel(F(c)) for F = J and I, directly by Mathlib PreservesKernel.iso and PreservesCokernel.iso. These constructions are already available from Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Abelian.Basic; no homology-preservation theorem is needed.

source.place: Tag 010N (lemma-exact-functor), kernel/equalizer argument and its cokernel dual; agent-written joint-detection assembly.

proof.text: For $F=J,I$, invertibility of $F(c)$ and $F(c)F(k)=0$ imply $F(k)=0$. The identity and zero endomorphisms of $F(K)$ then give the same factorization through the kernel arrow $F(k)$; kernel uniqueness gives $1_{F(K)}=0$. Likewise $F(q)F(c)=0$ gives $F(q)=0$, and cokernel uniqueness gives $1_{F(Q)}=0$. An object $T$ with $1_T=0$ is a zero object: every arrow $a:T\to A$ satisfies $a=a1_T=0$ and every $b:A\to T$ satisfies $b=1_Tb=0$, while zero arrows exist by preadditivity [def-sp-abelian]. Thus both $J(K),I(K)$ and both $J(Q),I(Q)$ are zero. Apply the assumed joint zero-object detection to $K$ and $Q$: both are zero objects. This writes out the elementary argument of Tag 00ZZ (lemma-preadditive-zero).

source.place: Tag 00ZZ (lemma-preadditive-zero), proof; definition-kernel and agent application of the joint-detection hypothesis.

proof.text: The zero kernel makes $c$ monic: if $ca=cb$, then $c(a-b)=0$, so $a-b$ factors through $k:K\to M$ by its universal property. Since $K$ is zero, this factorization is zero, hence $a=b$. The zero cokernel makes $c$ epic: if $ac=bc$, then $(a-b)c=0$, so $a-b$ factors through $q:N\to Q$ and is zero because $Q$ is zero. Differences and bilinearity of composition come from the preadditivity in [def-sp-abelian].

source.place: definition-kernel, kernel and cokernel universal properties; agent cancellation argument.

proof.text: By [def-sp-abelian], the monomorphism $c$ is a kernel of some map $h:N\to P$. Since $hc=0$ and $c$ is epic, $h=0$. The identity $1_N$ therefore factors through this kernel: there is $s:N\to M$ with $cs=1_N$. Now $c(sc)=c=c1_M$, and monicity of $c$ gives $sc=1_M$. Thus $s$ is a two-sided inverse of $c$, as required.
